entries.proposition: Design: three-site UK phase 2a, 15-week randomised double-blind placebo-controlled part A followed by an optional open-label part B, 24 randomised 2 to 1.
entries.snippet: The study comprised two parts (Figure 1A): part A was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study consisting of a screening period, a 3-week titration period, a 12-week maintenance period, and a taper period and/or follow-up

entries.proposition: Primary endpoint: change in mean 24-hour pain intensity on an 11-point numeric scale from baseline to week 15, from a three-times-daily electronic diary.
entries.snippet: The primary efficacy endpoint was change in mean 24-hour pain intensity NPS score (mean of three measurements collected during 1 day by electronic pain diary [E-diary]) from baseline to week 15 (end of part A).

entries.proposition: Power: 24 participants gave at least 65 percent power to detect a 2-point difference at a two-sided significance level of 0.10, a proof-of-concept design that could not exclude a modest effect.
entries.snippet: a sample size of 24 participants (with a randomization ratio of 2:1 for soticlestat: placebo) was judged to be sufficient to achieve at least 65% power to detect a 2-point difference between soticlestat and placebo

entries.proposition: The baseline pain score is derived from the last 7 days before screening, and participants were required to record pain scores for a minimum of 6 of 7 days before screening/enrollment (not before randomisation); the analysis defines 'baseline' as the part A baseline.
entries.snippet: Participants were required to record their pain intensity scores for a minimum of 6 of 7 days before screening/enrollment, and then three times per day throughout the study.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: The baseline is a 7-day mean of the diary scores before randomisation; the diary was required for at least 6 of 7 days before enrolment, a pre-dose baseline with measured completeness above 90 percent. The original said 7-day mean before randomisation and attached a measured completeness above 90 percent that this snippet does not carry (it is a separate Results sentence, now its own entry). The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: Primary result: change of minus 0.75 on drug and minus 0.41 on placebo, placebo-adjusted difference minus 0.34 with a 95 percent interval from minus 1.55 to 0.88 (P 0.570), reported as statistically non-significant. The interval includes zero and benefits up to 1.55 points on the 11-point scale, and it excludes the 2-point benefit the study was powered to detect; the authors say only that the planned power of at least 65 percent may have been too low.
entries.snippet: resulting in a statistically non-significant placebo-adjusted difference of –0.34 (–1.55, 0.88; P = .570)

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: Primary result: change of minus 0.75 on drug and minus 0.41 on placebo, placebo-adjusted difference minus 0.34 with an interval from minus 1.55 to 0.88 (P 0.570); the interval includes zero and effects up to about 1.5 points of benefit, but its lower end does not reach the 2-point difference the study was powered to detect, so it is an underpowered result and not a demonstration of no effect. The original said the lower end does not reach 2 points 'so it is an underpowered result'; that does not follow, because the interval excludes a 2-point benefit. The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: The placebo arm improved by 0.41 points on the primary scale and 2 of 9 placebo participants met the 30 percent responder definition, against 4 of 15 on drug.
entries.snippet: At week 15, four participants (26.7%) in the soticlestat group and two participants (22.2%) in the placebo group were classified as responders

entries.proposition: Global impression: improvement (much or minimally) at week 15 was reported by 7 of 15 on drug and 4 of 9 on placebo, i.e. 46.7 and 44.4 percent.
entries.snippet: An improvement in PGI-C status (much improved or minimally improved) from baseline to week 15 was reported by seven participants (46.7%) in the soticlestat group and four participants (44.4%) in the placebo group.

entries.proposition: At week 29, after all participants had received the drug, 12 of 18 (66.7 percent) reported improvement; the authors state this cannot be separated from placebo effects of being in a study.
entries.snippet: Similarly, the improvements noted in the PGI-C at week 29 must be interpreted with caution because they cannot be disentangled from the possible placebo effects associated with being in a clinical study.

entries.proposition: The pharmacodynamic marker fell: mean plasma 24-hydroxycholesterol decreased by about 70 percent in the first 2 weeks on drug and stayed low, while placebo values stayed at baseline.
entries.snippet: mean plasma 24HC levels decreased by approximately 70% in the first 2 weeks of treatment and remained at reduced levels throughout study parts A and B

entries.proposition: The authors say the plasma 24HC fall indicates that participants adhered to treatment and supports 24HC as a biomarker of soticlestat activity; in the same Discussion they say the study did not show significance for its primary endpoint.
entries.snippet: This indicates that participants adhered to treatment and supports the use of 24HC as a biomarker for soticlestat activity.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: The authors use the marker to infer adherence and that it supports use of 24HC as a biomarker of drug activity, while the clinical endpoint was null. The original called the clinical endpoint 'null', which is the reader's word; the source says the study did not show significance. The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: The authors say the open-label part B cannot be analysed statistically because there is no control arm.
entries.snippet: any potential treatment effect throughout part B could not be assessed statistically because of the lack of a control arm

entries.proposition: Imbalance despite randomisation: median time since symptom onset 11.3 versus 6.7 years and opioid use 73.3 versus 33.3 percent, drug versus placebo.
entries.snippet: However, some differences were observed in baseline clinical characteristics, with the soticlestat group having a median time since symptom onset of 11.3 years (range, 2.6–20.5 years) vs 6.7 years (range, 1.4–7.4 years) in the placebo group.

entries.proposition: The authors propose that the likelihood of a response may be greater in individuals at the onset of CRPS; this is their hypothesis about duration of disease, offered after a primary endpoint that did not reach significance.
entries.snippet: the likelihood of a response to soticlestat may be greater in individuals at the onset of CRPS

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: The authors propose the effect may be greater near onset, a duration-of-disease explanation offered after a null result. The original called the primary result 'a null result'; the source says lack of significance. The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table S2 prints mean PROMIS-29 physical-function scores by visit for different numbers of participants (baseline 15 on drug and 9 on placebo; part A 12 and 8): 34.65 and 35.83 at baseline, 36.38 and 38.51 at part A, 39.61 and 39.20 at part B. Means over different participants cannot be subtracted into a change; the paired changes to week 15 are printed in the main text as 2.4 on drug and 1.5 on placebo, so S2 does not show that the placebo arm rose more.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: Supplement Table S2: mean PROMIS-29 physical function at part A was 36.38 on drug and 38.51 on placebo from baselines of 34.65 and 35.83, i.e. the placebo arm rose more in the completers, while main Table 2 prints changes of 2.4 on drug and 1.5 on placebo. The original said 'the placebo arm rose more in the completers' by subtracting unmatched group means; the main table's paired changes run the other way (2.4 on drug, 1.5 on placebo).
